# Baruch Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Take off, O Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God.

**2** Clothe yourself in the double cloak of the righteousness that comes from God; and set on your head the diadem of the glory of the Eternal.

**3** For God will show your splendor to every nation under heaven.

**4** For your name will be called by God forever: Peace of Righteousness and Glory of Godliness.

**5** Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on the height, and look toward the east, and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.

**6** For they went out from you on foot, led away by enemies; but God is bringing them back to you, borne in glory as if on a royal throne.

**7** For God has commanded that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and the valleys filled up, to level the ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.

**8** The woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel at God's command.

**9** For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.

---
*LOGOS notes: v.2 "double cloak" renders Greek diploidia accurately — this is a double garment or folded cloak, a mark of honor and wealth (cf. 1 Sam 2:19 variant readings). v.4 the divine name is a formal decree: "Peace of Righteousness / Glory of Godliness" — rendered with capital letters in consensus to indicate it as a formal name. v.7 the Isaiah 40 echo is unmistakable: the leveling of mountains and filling of valleys in preparation for the return. Luke 3:4-6 cites Isa 40:3-5 in precisely this context; Baruch seems to draw on the same tradition, whether independently or as a mediating text. v.8 "fragrant tree" — Greek euōdes = sweet-smelling; the trees provide shade and scent for the returning exiles.*
